The Rainbow
RAYN-boh
noun (a covenant sign)
From Old English regnboga, rain-bow; the Hebrew qesheth, a bow, the same word used of the weapon of war, here set down in token of peace.

📖 Biblical Definition

The Rainbow is the bow set in the cloud, the appointed token of the covenant God made with Noah and with all flesh after the flood. "I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth" (Gen 9:13). The Hebrew word is the word for a bow of war, yet here the bow is unstrung and turned upward, a weapon laid aside—God's pledge that He will never again destroy the earth by the waters of a flood. As often as the bow appears in the clouds, God says, He will remember His everlasting covenant (9:16). It is therefore a sign of His covenant faithfulness and of His common-grace preservation of a guilty world. The same bow encircles the throne of God in glory: "and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald" (Rev 4:3). This dictionary confesses the rainbow as a divine token of mercy and faithfulness; and it notes honestly the modern co-opting of the rainbow as a banner for what Scripture calls sin, and labors to recover the bow as God's own covenant sign, not man's emblem of rebellion.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The bow set in the cloud as the token of the Noahic covenant, God's pledge never again to drown the earth by flood; the same bow rings the throne in glory. It is a sign of covenant faithfulness and common-grace preservation.

expand to see more

THE RAINBOW, noun. The arc of color in the cloud, appointed by God as the token of His covenant with Noah and all flesh.

The Hebrew names a bow of war, here laid aside as a pledge of peace between God and the earth.

"I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth" (Gen 9:13).

It requires of man the remembrance of God's faithfulness and forbids the despair that fears another universal flood.

Its highest sense is the bow round about the throne, the token of mercy in the very presence of judgment.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 9:13 — "I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth."

Gen 9:16 — "And the bow shall be in the cloud; and I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth."

Gen 9:12 — "And God said, This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:"

Rev 4:3 — "And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The rainbow has been co-opted in the modern age as a banner for what Scripture names as sin; the doctrine recovers it as God's own covenant token of mercy and faithfulness.

expand to see more

In the present age the rainbow has been seized by the progressive movement as the emblem of pride and of sexual identities and practices that Scripture plainly names as sin. The bow that God set in the cloud as a pledge of His faithfulness has been turned into a banner of human rebellion, waved precisely against the moral order the covenant God upholds. This is a theft and an inversion: the sign of divine mercy made the standard of defiance.

The church recovers the rainbow by remembering whose bow it is. It was God who set it, God who reads it, God who remembers His covenant when it appears. The bow is unstrung and aimed upward, the arrow of judgment withheld—a mercy, not a license. To recover the sign is to confess that the One who spared the world from flood will yet judge it by fire, and that His patience now is the space He gives for repentance, not for pride.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew qesheth, a bow of war here laid aside as a token of peace, the sign of the Noahic covenant.

expand to see more

Qesheth, Hebrew, a bow; the same word for the weapon of war, here turned to a token of mercy.

Regnboga, Old English, rain-bow, the arc of color appearing after rain.

Oth, Hebrew, a sign or token, as the rainbow is the token of the covenant.

The Noahic covenant, made with Noah and all flesh, of which the bow is the perpetual sign.

The bow about the throne in Revelation, the token of mercy set in the place of judgment.

Usage

"He taught his children that the rainbow is God's covenant token, not the world's banner of pride."

"When the storm passed and the rainbow appeared, she remembered the covenant God made with Noah."

"The pastor reclaimed the rainbow from its modern co-opting, preaching it as the sign of mercy and faithfulness."
